author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Test a USB drive as temporary EmuCoreX library storage
summary: Qualify an OTG adapter, power path, filesystem, document-tree grant, sustained reads, and safe eject behavior with copied test images while keeping emulator data and the verified source elsewhere.
heroAlt: Rufus removable-drive selection screen illustrating the need to identify the exact USB target before a storage test

blocks.text: Qualify the USB chain before selecting a library folder

A USB drive connected through OTG adds several failure points: phone port, adapter, hub power, cable, filesystem driver, document provider, and the drive itself. Treat it as a temporary working root, not as the location for BIOS, memory cards, save states, or the only copy of a personal dump. A test should prove that the drive survives sustained reads and Android lifecycle changes without disconnecting.

Never unplug storage while a game, scan, hash, copy, or save-related operation is active. Android may cache writes, and an unannounced removal can damage the filesystem even when the game images are intended to be read-only.
Assemble a low-risk USB test set

items: A known-good OTG adapter or powered hub compatible with the phone.
One small and one large verified personal PS2 image copied from a preserved source.
A filesystem the current Android build can mount read-write.
SHA-256 and byte sizes recorded before connection.
Battery and power conditions that will not trigger an OTG shutdown during the session.

blocks.text: Exercise mount, scan, load, and eject

items: 1. Connect the empty or backed-up drive and wait for Android to report it as available.
2. Use the system Files app to create and delete a harmless test file, proving the provider is writable before copying library data.
3. Copy the two test images to one dedicated PS2 folder and compare their hashes with the source records.
4. Add that exact folder to EmuCoreX through Android's tree picker; do not grant the entire USB volume.
5. Refresh once, cold-boot both titles, and play through a long loading sequence on the larger image.
6. Return to the library, close the running game normally, and force-stop EmuCoreX.
7. Use Android's eject action and wait for confirmation before disconnecting the cable.
8. Reconnect, authorize again only if Android requires it, and repeat one cold boot to test mount identity.

blocks.text: A drive that works in the Files app can still brown out during sustained reads. Hubs without adequate power, mechanical disks, and simultaneous controller or audio devices increase demand. If the USB device repeatedly remounts, move the test image back to internal storage before changing emulator settings.
Keep a short record because success can depend on the exact adapter, Android build, and power state.

items: Both destination hashes match the verified source copies.
The larger title completes a sustained-load scene without provider errors.
Force-stop does not make the folder vanish before physical removal.
Android eject completes before disconnection.
Reconnect does not create duplicate parent and child roots.
Drive disconnects when loading begins: investigate power, adapter, cable, and device temperature.
Android mounts read-only: do not attempt library repair inside EmuCoreX.
Hash changes after reconnect: retire that destination copy and inspect media health.
Permission returns but files do not: the provider may expose a different volume identity or cloud placeholder.

blocks.text: Return the test titles to stable storage

Remove the USB folder grant from EmuCoreX, refresh once, and re-enable the untouched internal test root. Eject the drive through Android, preserve its error information, and delete no verified source. Emulator data requires no restoration because it never belonged on the temporary drive.
OTG support is not uniform across phones

Some devices disable USB host mode at low battery, while others cannot power a drive and controller together. Desktop-class filesystem support also varies. Document the whole chain instead of calling a drive universally compatible after one menu launch.
